title.narrative: Integrated Multisector Assistance for Drought-Affected Communities in Saba Boru, Wadara and Aga Wayu Woredas of Guji Zone, Oromia, Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtInternational Medical Corps UK*nbsplt/pgtltpgtInternational Medical Corps (IMC) is a US-registered independent affiliate organization of International Medical Corps UK (IMC UK), with which IMC UK shares the same name and charitable objectives and mission. IMC UK and IMC work together to deliver assistance programs in an accountable and effective manner in pursuit of their commonly held charitable objectives. IMC UK will engage IMC to implement its programmes in the field, with IMC UK oversight, according to the terms and conditions of the agreement that results from this proposal and the terms of the parties’ administrative service agreement. Together with IMC Croatia, IMC provides administrative and operational support to IMC UK and to the programmes on the ground, including but not limited to financial management, banking and cash management, procurement management/international procurements and logistics.nbspThis project focuses on addressing urgent life-saving needs in Saba Boru, Aga Wayu, and Wadera woreda, regions severely impacted by drought. Access to essential services from humanitarian partners and government structures is critically limited in these areas. This multi-sectoral response aligns with the Second Reserve Allocation 2024 – Anticipatory Action initiative, integrating Health, Nutrition, and WASH sectors to meet the diverse needs of affected communities. The aim of this initiative is to provide dignified, rights-based humanitarian assistance that addresses immediate needs while promoting safe access to essential services. The project emphasizes a well-coordinated response that integrates gender considerations, protection measures, accountability to affected populations (AAP), and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA).nbspThrough health interventions, IMC aims to reach approximately 23,400 beneficiaries by offering free and comprehensive primary health care services. This will involve deploying three MHNTs focused on maternal and child health, enhancing routine and emergency immunization efforts, supporting disease surveillance, training local health care providers, and ensuring health facilities are operational with adequate supplies and equipment. Services will include integrated comprehensive MHPSS, family planning counseling, ANC, PNC, syndromic treatment of STIs, and CMR/IPV. The protection component will prioritize assistance for IDPs to mitigate their vulnerability to risks and human rights violations.nbspThe nutrition intervention will implement lifesaving measures by integrating CMAM and IYCF-E activities through the existing health systems. To avert the emergency humanitarian situation related to the aggravating factors in the proposed Woredas, the nutrition program will prioritize the Nutrition specific (treatment of acute malnutrition, IYCF and SBC) and Nutrition sensitive (FSL, hygiene promotion and MPC) interventions integrated with health, MHPSS, and protection targeted to most vulnerable beneficiaries. The nutrition activities shall involve all the stakeholders from the program design up to the end of the project life through project cycle management.nbspThe WASH interventionnbspwill cover the critical needs among drought and conflict-affected people by increasing access to WASH services throughnbsprehabilitation and maintenance of 6 existing water systems, 1nbsppond construction, and 3nbsproof rainwater harvesting, maintaining six blocks (6 blocks, each has six rooms) gender, age, and disability-appropriate sanitation facilities (latrines), installation of 6 hand washing facilities, distribution of 9000 WASH NFIs through cash transfer, capacity building for 42 WASHCO members, hygiene promotion in the three targeted woredas to reach 30,000 individuals and environmental health-solid waste management at three health facilities. The project plans to reach a total of 156,573 people directly andnbsp166,955 indirectly. With a total budget of USD 700,000, the project will be implemented from Novembernbsp1, 2024 - April 30, 2025.nbsplt/pgt
